rounds.text: Durlax Top Surface Ltd trades at an exceptionally modest P/E ratio of 12x [E1] and a P/B of 1.31x [E2], representing a steep discount compared to sector benchmarks of 32.71x and 2.76x respectively [E6, E7]. This valuation disconnect stands in stark contrast to the company's remarkable financial performance, which features a 5-year compounded sales growth of 57% [E14] and a 5-year compounded profit growth of 77% [E17]. Recent quarters demonstrate an acceleration of this fundamental strength, highlighted by a trailing twelve-month sales growth of 51% [E16], profit growth of 69% [E19], and an impressive rules-based screen score of 96 out of 100 [E56]. Furthermore, a discounted cash flow model suggests a massive intrinsic value of ₹ 183 per share against a market price of ₹ 52.6 [E39], offering a 71.3% margin of safety [E40] where today's price implies a negligible earnings growth of just 0.7% [E41]. Conceded: promoter holding has decreased over recent periods to 51.45% [E35, E55] and operating cash flow for Mar 2026 is negative at Rs -12 Cr [E28, E29]. Operating margins remain inconsistent [E26, E27], and the business currently offers a 0.00% dividend yield [E4, E54].
